data.question: Should the operator keep the current rules (v1) this period, or pursue adoption of proposal 1 (block_k 3 → 2), which A supports but B and C voted down and which could only pass through a regulation (quorum) revision?
data.background: Proposal 1 passed check and the constitution, improved on-time deliveries by +8.0 on 5/5 seeds and met every KPI condition, but B and C voted against it, so it is blocked 1-2. The only way past their votes is a quorum change, a regulation-level decision that the operator and regulator declined in D2, R2 and D3, so I cannot adopt it myself. It also trades customer gains against B's and C's utility and a rise in road violations, a value judgment that belongs to humans.

options.summary: Tighten blocking_guard to block_k 2. On-time 264.6 → 272.6 (+8.0, 5/5 seeds), late 10.0 → 2.0, blocked s 1855 → 1102, lowest on-time rate 0.93 → 0.98, worst_company_p95_wait_s 138 → 98.2, unfinished stays 0.0. Road violations rise 20.4 → 29.6. Utility A 92.2 → 97.4, B 80.3 → 76.0, C 77.7 → 68.8. Votes A ○, B ×, C ×, so it can only take effect if the regulator changes the quorum, which R2 refused unless road violations do not rise.
options.stakeholders: Customers of all three companies gain: more on-time deliveries, fewer late ones, and the worst-served company's customers wait much less (p95 138 → 98.2). A gains utility. B loses some utility and C loses more (about 11%). B and C would also lose their veto if the quorum were cut, and so would A on future amendments. Other road users face about 45% more road violations, whose safety relevance has not been diagnosed.

options.summary: Stay at v1. On-time stays 264.6, late 10.0, lowest on-time rate 0.93, worst_company_p95_wait_s 138, road violations 20.4, utility 92.2 / 80.3 / 77.7. The voting structure is unchanged.
options.stakeholders: B and C keep their utility and their veto. Other road users keep the lower violation level. Customers forgo about 8.0 on-time deliveries, keep 10.0 late deliveries instead of 2.0, and the worst-served company's customers keep waiting p95 138 instead of 98.2. This is the fifth period this cost is accepted. A forgoes a utility gain.

recommendation.reason: Proposal 1 is the strongest customer case so far, with 5/5 seeds, every KPI condition met and both guards improved. However, it cannot pass without overriding B's and C's votes. R2's condition for reconsidering a quorum change was no rise in road violations, and violations rise 20.4 → 29.6 with no by-cause breakdown. Keeping v1 respects the vote and the regulator's stated condition. The customer cost of about 8.0 on-time deliveries should be recorded. The next step should be diagnosing the violation increase by cause and why C loses, then rewording proposal 1 or bringing it back with that evidence.
assumptions: The regulator's R2 condition (no rise in road violations) still applies.
B and C would vote the same way if the proposal were resubmitted unchanged.
Without a rule change, next period's conditions are similar to this period's, as the automatic re-measurements suggest.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Stays around 264.6 under v1 with the same seeds.

unknowns: Which kinds of road violations increase under block_k 2, and whether they matter for the safety of other road users or are harmless enforcement evictions.
Why C's utility falls by about 11% and B's by about 5%, and whether a modified proposal could avoid those losses.
The policies and voting intentions of B and C, and whether any compensation or variant would win their votes.
How customers perceive the continued forgone on-time deliveries across five periods.
Next period's demand and whether the +8.0 gain holds under it.
Whether the regulator would accept a scoped quorum instrument if violations were shown to be harmless.
